concepts.def: A pole is a place on a magnet where the magnetic forces are strongest. A bar magnet has two: a north (seeking) pole and a south (seeking) pole, one at each end.
Like poles are two poles of the same kind (N and N, or S and S) and they repel each other. Unlike poles are one north and one south, and they attract each other.
A force that acts between two objects that are not touching. Attraction and repulsion between two magnetic poles are examples of non-contact force.
A magnet that produces its own magnetic field. It keeps that field whether or not any other magnet is nearby, and it has a fixed north pole and south pole.

A material that becomes a magnet when it is placed in a magnetic field. Induced magnetism always causes a force of attraction, and when the material is removed from the field it loses most or all of its magnetism quickly.
The region around a magnet where a force acts on another magnet or on a magnetic material.
A material on which a magnet exerts a force of attraction. The specification names iron, steel, cobalt and nickel.
The strength of the magnetic field depends on the distance from the magnet: it is strongest at the poles and gets weaker as the distance from the magnet increases.
The direction of the magnetic field at any point is the direction of the force that would act on another north pole placed at that point.

A line used to represent a magnetic field. Its direction is from the north (seeking) pole of a magnet to the south (seeking) pole of the magnet, and lines drawn closer together represent a stronger field.
An instrument containing a small bar magnet that is free to turn. The needle lines up with, and points in the direction of, the magnetic field it sits in.
The Earth has a magnetic field, and a compass needle placed away from other magnets points in the direction of the Earth's magnetic field.

A method of finding a field pattern: place a compass near the magnet, mark a dot at each end of the needle, move the compass so its tail sits on the previous head dot, repeat, then join the dots into a line and add an arrow.

A compass points the same way anywhere on the Earth's surface with no magnet nearby. The field must therefore be produced by the Earth itself, which is evidence that the core of the Earth must be magnetic.

mcqs.q: The north pole of one bar magnet is brought close to the north pole of a second bar magnet. What happens to the magnets?
options: They repel each other, because the two poles are alike
They attract, because magnets always pull each other
Nothing happens until the two magnets are touching
They repel only if one of the magnets is stronger
mcqs.explain: Two like poles repel each other, so two north poles push apart.

mcqs.q: Two magnets on a bench push each other apart while there is still a 2 cm gap between them. Which statement best describes this force?
options: It is a contact force passed through the bench surface
It is a non-contact force, acting across the air gap
It is a non-contact force only while they move
It is a contact force acting through the air
mcqs.explain: Attraction and repulsion between two magnetic poles are examples of non-contact force, so the force acts over a distance.

mcqs.q: A steel paper clip is held near a strong magnet and becomes magnetic itself. What name is given to the paper clip while it is in the field?
options: The clip is a permanent magnet
The clip is a non-magnetic metal
The clip is an induced magnet
The clip is a magnetic pole
mcqs.explain: An induced magnet is a material that becomes a magnet when it is placed in a magnetic field.

mcqs.q: A chain of paper clips hangs from a bar magnet. The magnet is taken away. What happens to the paper clips?
options: They stay in a chain, now permanently magnetic
They push each other apart and scatter widely
They stay in a chain for the next few hours
They lose their magnetism and fall apart
mcqs.explain: When removed from the magnetic field an induced magnet loses most or all of its magnetism quickly.

mcqs.q: The south pole of one bar magnet is brought near the north pole of another. Which row correctly describes the force?
options: Repulsion, because these two poles are different
Attraction, because unlike poles attract each other
Attraction, because south poles always attract
No force at all, as the poles are not alike
mcqs.explain: Two unlike poles attract each other, and this happens for any pair of N and S poles.

mcqs.q: A student wants two magnets on trolleys to push apart when released. How should the magnets be arranged?
options: With a north pole facing a south pole
With the two magnets touching end to end
With two north poles facing each other
With one magnet turned on its side
mcqs.explain: Two like poles repel each other, so N facing N gives a push apart.

mcqs.q: Which statement gives a correct difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet?
options: An induced magnet keeps its magnetism when it is removed
A permanent magnet can only ever attract things
An induced magnet has a fixed north pole and south pole
A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field
mcqs.explain: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field, while an induced magnet only becomes magnetic in a field.

mcqs.q: An iron nail is brought near the south pole of a magnet and is pulled in. The magnet is then turned round so the north pole faces the nail. What happens?
options: The nail is still pulled towards the magnet
The nail is pushed away, as the pole has changed
The nail is pushed away only when it is close
The nail now feels no force from this new pole
mcqs.explain: The force between a magnet and a magnetic material is always one of attraction, whichever pole faces it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of a magnetic field?
options: The set of lines drawn on a diagram around a bar magnet
The area a magnet covers when it is touching an object
The region around a magnet where a force acts on another magnet
The space that fills with force once iron is placed in it
mcqs.explain: The magnetic field is the region around a magnet where a force acts on another magnet or on a magnetic material.

mcqs.q: A magnet is held over a tray containing a copper coin, a nickel disc, an aluminium strip and a steel screw. Which objects are attracted?
options: All four of them, since they are all metals
The copper coin and the steel screw
Only the steel screw and nothing else
Only the nickel disc and the steel screw
mcqs.explain: Nickel and steel are magnetic materials; copper and aluminium are not.

mcqs.q: A bar magnet is brought near an unmagnetised iron bar. The magnet is then flipped end for end. Which statement about the force on the iron bar is correct?
options: It stays an attraction, whichever pole faces the bar
It now changes from an attraction to a strong repulsion
It becomes zero, because the two poles now cancel out
It stays a repulsion for each of the two poles
mcqs.explain: The force between a magnet and a magnetic material is always one of attraction.

mcqs.q: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?
options: In the middle of the magnet
At the poles of the magnet
Equally strong at every point
At the outer ends of the lines
mcqs.explain: The field is strongest at the poles of the magnet.

mcqs.q: A plotting compass is moved slowly away from the north pole of a bar magnet. What happens to the magnetic field where the compass is?
options: It stays exactly the same until a definite edge is reached
It gets stronger as the compass moves away from the pole
It stays the same all the way around the bar magnet
It gets weaker, because the distance from the magnet increases
mcqs.explain: The strength of the magnetic field depends on the distance from the magnet, so moving away weakens it.

mcqs.q: Outside a bar magnet, which way do the magnetic field lines point?
options: From the north pole to the south pole
From the south pole across to the north
From each pole in towards the middle
Always straight out from each pole
mcqs.explain: The direction of a magnetic field line is from the north (seeking) pole of a magnet to the south (seeking) pole.

mcqs.q: A compass is placed at a point in the field of a bar magnet. What does the direction the needle's north end points in tell you?
options: The straight line from that point to the nearest pole
The direction of the magnetic field at that point
The direction the compass would travel if released
The way that a south pole would be pushed there
mcqs.explain: The direction of the field at any point is the direction of the force that would act on another north pole placed at that point.

mcqs.q: What is inside a magnetic compass?
options: A light piece of iron
A coil of thin wire
A small bar magnet
A drop of liquid metal
mcqs.explain: A magnetic compass contains a small bar magnet, free to turn.

mcqs.q: A compass is placed on a bench with no magnets anywhere near it. What does the needle do?
options: It settles pointing along the Earth's own magnetic field
It keeps spinning slowly, as there is no field present
It points towards the coldest part of the whole room
It points straight downwards towards the floor
mcqs.explain: The Earth has a magnetic field, and the compass needle points in the direction of the Earth's magnetic field.

mcqs.q: A student is plotting the field pattern of a bar magnet using a plotting compass. Which method is correct?
options: Slide the compass all the way round the magnet while touching it
Mark a dot at each end of the needle, then move the compass on
Draw a straight line from the compass to the nearest pole
Put the compass down and draw round the outside of it
mcqs.explain: Marking both ends and moving the compass so its tail sits on the last head dot builds up one field line, which is then joined and given an arrow.

mcqs.q: A student draws the field pattern of a bar magnet. Which feature of the drawing shows that the field is stronger near the poles?
options: The lines are drawn a long way apart there
The lines are drawn with two arrows on them
The lines are drawn closer together there
The lines are drawn longer at the poles
mcqs.explain: Lines drawn closer together represent a stronger field, and they are most crowded at the poles.

mcqs.q: A compass points the same way on a bench, in a field and out at sea, with no magnets nearby. What does this suggest about the Earth?
options: The ice at the North Pole acts like a magnet
The atmosphere is what pulls the needle
The Earth's gravity is turning the needle
The core of the Earth must be magnetic
mcqs.explain: A field present everywhere with no magnet nearby must be produced by the Earth itself, which is evidence that the core of the Earth must be magnetic.
